data.title: clicking on a shape tool that is already selected should toggle between filled and border only shape drawing

data.body:
Implemented in 5 commits (5198625, 605f6fd, 62d6fcc, 1a28ab0, 480685c), exactly per plan; no deviations.

1. raster: private ellipseSamples extracted from ellipseOutline (byte- and order-identical output verified against the pre-refactor function over every box 0..40 x 0..40 plus reversed/negative corners); new rectFilled and ellipseFilled, both emitting solely through plot(x,y).
2. state: AppState.shapeFill (session-only, per-tool), initialised { rect: false, ellipse: false }.
3. tools: Tool.fillable?: true, ToolContext.filled (live getter on toolCtx), makeShapeTool takes an optional filled raster and picks per draw call; rect/ellipse pass theirs.
4. interaction + indicators in one commit: setTool re-click branch -> toggleShapeFill (plain store.set, no dirty bumps), e.repeat guard scoped to the tool-hotkey branch, tips, toolbar data-fill/aria-label/title via setAttribute only, .tool[data-fill=on] svg { fill: currentColor }, LCD 'tool filled'.
5. BRANDING.md §6 clause.

Verification: npx tsc --noEmit and npm run build clean after every step. No browser available, so pure logic was smoke-checked in a scratchpad harness (not committed): filled rect/ellipse span coverage, per-row contiguity, x/y symmetry, filled output a superset of outline output, degenerate 1x1 / 1xN / zero-height cases; plot-contract checks asserting a border-style plot drops locked-center and out-of-bounds pixels and a mod() plot wraps tile coordinates for both filled primitives; shape-tool checks (fillable flags, outline vs filled drag output, mid-drag flip, line unaffected); a stubbed-DOM toolbar check (data-fill only on rect/ellipse, seeded off, sync never touches innerHTML so the .led survives, aria-pressed still means active).

Acceptance criteria: code-verified 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 (state side), 7, 11, 12, 14; verified at the plot-contract level but needing a browser to confirm end to end 8, 9, 10; needing a browser 2, 13, 15 (visual/LCD width). Untouched as required: persist.ts, history.ts, doc.ts, selection.ts, preview/*, export/*, tools/line.ts. Left another agent's uncommitted .lattice changes for task_01KZP5W6 alone.

REVIEW (cold, fresh context) — PASS, moving to done. No rework needed, no inline fixes required.

Reviewed: commits 5198625, 605f6fd, 62d6fcc, 1a28ab0, 480685c against the plan's sections 1-7 and its 15 acceptance criteria. Read the full current text of all 12 changed files plus the pre-change raster.ts (5198625~1), grid-editor's pointer/ToolContext plumbing, the preview + autosave subscriptions, and the keydown handler in full. Ran my own harnesses (scratchpad, not committed), independent of the implementer's.

MECHANICAL
- npx tsc --noEmit: clean. npm run build: clean (34 modules, 38.71 kB js / 7.82 kB css).
- npm run dev on :5174 (5173 was already taken by someone else's server — I started and killed only my own pid, nothing else touched); index.html, /src/main.ts and the transformed app.css all serve, and the served CSS contains the .tool[data-fill="on"] svg rule.

INDEPENDENT HARNESSES (mine, ~1.98M assertions total, 0 failures)
1. ellipseOutline refactor is behaviour-preserving: 215,296 bounding boxes (x0,y0 in -3..12, w,h in -14..14, i.e. reversed and negative corners included) compared as ORDERED plot sequences against the pre-refactor function extracted from 5198625~1. Byte- and order-identical everywhere. rectOutline likewise unchanged. The degenerate guard changed shape (w===0||hgt===0 -> rx===lx||by===ty) but is arithmetically the same predicate, and the sequence comparison covers it.
2. Filled is a superset of outline, silhouettes agree: for every box 0..40 x 0..40, every outline pixel is in the filled set, no filled pixel escapes the bbox, every row is gap-free, and the touched rows are a contiguous span. Repeated at realistic and beyond-realistic sizes (1..576 per axis; MAX_CELL=64 so the real ceiling is L=192) at three origins including negative ones (the focused-tile raw margin): rows covered == bbox height exactly, x extent == lx..rx exactly, no outline pixel uncovered. No sampling gaps at any aspect ratio.
3. rectFilled area is exactly (|dx|+1)*(|dy|+1); a 1x1 drag plots exactly one pixel. Degenerate ellipse drags (zero width, zero height, single point) emit the identical sequence to ellipseOutline and to the normalized line(). x- and y-symmetry hold for the filled ellipse.
4. Plot contract (the load-bearing constraint, section 4.1): driving both filled primitives with a border-style plot that drops out-of-bounds and locked-center writes lets nothing through and throws nothing; driving them with a mod() tile plot yields exactly the 64 wrapped cells of an 8x8 seam-straddling rect and never an out-of-cell coordinate. Confirms neither primitive writes a buffer, bounds-checks itself, or wraps itself.
5. Non-integer inputs never produce non-integer output coordinates.
6. Toolbar under a stub DOM whose innerHTML setter WIPES children (so any innerHTML write in sync would be caught): data-fill is seeded "off" on rect/ellipse only and is absent on pencil/eraser/line/fill/eyedropper/select; after 500 alternating syncs every key still has exactly one .led and its icon markup; aria-pressed still tracks the active tool only; aria-label/title flip to "rect filled"/"rect filled (r)" and back; per-tool independence holds; a missing shapeFill entry reads as off.

PLAN CONSTRAINTS — all verified
- setTool: the !== branch is byte-identical to before (git diff confirms only the inside of the early return changed), so genuine tool CHANGES still commitFloatFirst() then clearSelectionPatch() in the same order. This was the highest-risk edit and it is clean.
- Re-click toggle vs PM-7 float: sel.float is assigned in exactly one place (main.ts:203, inside pasteClip, after its forced setTool("select")), so a fillable tool can never be active with a live float. Reaching rect from select goes through the !== branch and stamps first. Correct, and it does not depend on that invariant.
- e.repeat guard is inside the "if (tool)" branch only: undo (ctrl/meta, returns earlier), z/1/2, escape, enter, arrows and the delete branch are all untouched, and typing in PM-6's cell-size input returns at the top of the handler on target.tagName === "INPUT" before the guard is ever reached.
- toggleShapeFill is a plain store.set of { shapeFill, tip }. The preview subscription keys on dirtyPreview/mode/dirtyDoc and the autosave subscription on dirtyDoc/dirtyPreview/mode/colorHex — neither fires. No bumpSel, no history.push. shapeFill is absent from persist.ts and from the project schema.
- ctx.filled is a live getter reading shapeFill[store.get().tool]; grid-editor re-reads deps.getTool() on every pointer event, so the flag and the tool receiving the event are always the same tool — no stale or mismatched read during a drag. makeShapeTool picks the raster per draw() call, so preview and commit agree.
- CSS: .tool[data-fill="on"] svg { fill: currentColor } sits after .key svg (which sets no fill) and is the only fill rule in the sheet. Presentation attributes lose to every author rule in the cascade, so it beats the svg root's fill="none"; the rect/ellipse glyphs carry no per-shape fill attribute so they inherit the override, and neither key can pick up a multi-path icon.
- Untouched as required: persist.ts, history.ts, doc.ts, selection.ts, preview/*, export/*, tools/line.ts (git diff over the whole range is empty for all of them). transport.ts is untouched so PM-9's export-scale stepper is unaffected; toolbar.sync's cell readout path is unchanged so PM-6's stepper is unaffected.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1 build clean — verified by build. 2 toggle visible — verified by code + shim (attrs/LCD/tips); pixel appearance needs a browser. 3 filled output — verified by code. 4 live preview fills — verified by code. 5 one undo entry — verified by code (beginStroke only in onDown). 6 per-tool independence — verified by code + shim. 7 line inert — verified by code + shim. 8 border clips silently — verified at the plot-contract level; end-to-end PNG needs a browser. 9 tile wraps — plot-contract verified; browser for the preview/export. 10 focus wraps — plot-contract verified with negative-origin boxes; browser for the visual. 11 silhouettes agree — verified by code, exhaustively. 12 degenerate drags — verified by code. 13 hotkey parity, no strobe — verified by code. 14 inert everywhere else — verified by code (subscriptions traced). 15 brand audit — verified by code for tokens/colors/copy and BRANDING section 6; the visual (ink-on-plastic vs orange-on-charcoal, LED, depress, focus ring) needs a browser.
Nothing is unverifiable in principle; 2, 8, 9, 10, 13, 15 have a residual visual/end-to-end half that requires a human at a browser, which section 8 always intended.

OBSERVATIONS (no action taken, not defects in this change)
- LCD width: "ellipse filled" adds ~7 monospace chars. There is headroom at desktop widths; below the 880px breakpoint the strip already overflows its readouts before this change, so this worsens an existing condition rather than creating one. Worth a glance at a narrow window during the human pass.
- Pre-existing and explicitly out of scope here: the z / 1 / 2 key branches have no e.repeat guard, so holding z strobes focus. On the record only; not introduced by PM-10.
- ctx.filled calls store.get() twice, matching the style of plot/erase/fill in the same object literal. Left alone.
- Left another agent's uncommitted .lattice changes for task_01KZP5W6 alone.

Verdict: meets every acceptance criterion establishable without a browser, with no deviations from the plan and no defects found. Moving to done.
